name: What is the purpose of priming siding before painting?

mainEntity.name: What is the purpose of priming siding before painting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Priming siding serves several crucial purposes before painting. It creates a uniform surface for the topcoat, improving paint adhesion and preventing issues like peeling or blistering. Primer also seals the siding material, which is especially important for porous surfaces like wood, controlling absorption and ensuring an even finish. Additionally, it can block stains, knots, and sap from bleeding through the final paint layers. For new or bare siding, priming is essential for durability and a professional-looking result. It enhances the longevity of the paint system and provides better coverage.
acceptedAnswer.description: Priming siding creates a uniform surface for paint adhesion, seals the material, and blocks stains, contributing to a durable and even finish.
